name: Rossell Techsys Ltd
tagline: Defence/aerospace interconnect and MRO supplier (demerged from Rossell India) riding India's defence-indigenization wave with a Rs 800 Cr order book (5.2x quarterly revenue) and a new global-semiconductor-OEM diversification, but ROCE remains weak (~7-8%), margins are still below management's own 15-22% guided band, leverage is high (~6.5x net debt/EBITDA pre-raise) and the stock trades at an extreme ~196x trailing P/E / ~33x book.
business_overview: Rossell Techsys Ltd (NSE/BSE: ROSSTECH), demerged from Rossell India Ltd (spun off Aug 2024, listed separately Dec 9 2024), supplies interconnect solutions, limited manufacturing services, repair/rework of electrical panels and sub-assemblies, and test/after-market services for military-aerospace and defence platforms. Traces to a 2008 Rossell India division (Vankesh Avionics Technologies, renamed Rossell Techsys in 2011). Newly diversifying: onboarded a major global semiconductor OEM after a qualification process, with revenue expected from Q2 FY27. Entity confirmed via screener.in (ticker ROSSTECH). Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@rishithegreat41, medium conviction).
fundamentals_table: Rs 154.7 Cr / net profit Rs 6.98 Cr (+134.5% YoY); EBITDA Rs 23.3 Cr (+95% YoY), EBITDA margin ~15.1%
FY24-FY26 revenue Rs 217 Cr -> Rs 260 Cr -> Rs 485 Cr (revenue nearly doubled in FY26); Q1 FY27 +78% YoY (Rs 87 Cr -> Rs 155 Cr)
3-yr avg ROCE ~7.8% (a Q2 FY26 print as low as ~6.0%); returns have not caught up with the revenue growth story

Borrowings ~Rs 409 Cr FY26 (up from Rs 240 Cr FY25, Rs 168 Cr FY24); net debt/EBITDA ~6.5x; D/E ~1.8x - a Rs 300 Cr preferential equity raise to SBI Mutual Fund was board-approved 18-Sep-26 (EGM 15-Oct-26) to address this
~196x trailing P/E, ~33x price-to-book (price Rs 1,374 vs book value Rs 41.1)
~69.9% currently (down from 74.8%) after a ~4.9% block-deal sale to Kotak Mutual Fund for Rs 166.23 Cr; no pledge
fundamentals_narrative: Revenue growth remains extraordinary and reflects a real structural tailwind - India's defence-indigenization push - now reinforced by a newly-announced diversification into the global semiconductor supply chain (a major OEM onboarded after qualification, revenue expected from Q2 FY27). Q1 FY27 revenue grew 78% YoY to Rs154.7 Cr with EBITDA up 95% YoY to Rs23.3 Cr (margin ~15.1%, at the low end of management's newly-stated 15-22% long-term guided band and an improvement on FY26's quarterly range of ~11-13%). But profitability still has not caught up with growth: 3-year average ROCE is only ~7.8% (a Q2 FY26 print of ~6.0% was flagged by one source as value-destructive), net margin is thin, and leverage remains high (borrowings ~Rs409 Cr FY26, net debt/EBITDA ~6.5x, D/E ~1.8x) after two capacity expansions (Rs70 Cr Nov-2025 + Rs30 Cr May-2026, ~360,000 sq ft combined) funded mostly by debt/accruals. The company is now addressing the leverage directly: the board approved a Rs300 Cr preferential equity issue to SBI Mutual Fund on 18-Sep-2026 (EGM scheduled 15-Oct-2026), which - if it completes - would meaningfully de-risk the balance sheet. Separately, the promoter family sold a ~4.9% stake via block deal to Kotak Mutual Fund (promoter holding now ~69.9%, still high, no pledge). The stock already trades at ~196x trailing P/E and ~33x book value - an extreme multiple that prices in a profitability inflection the primary numbers have only just started to show in Q1 FY27.
technical_read: Market cap up further since the prior pass; shares have gained ~101% over six months per one Sept-16 2026 report, reflecting the growth re-rating plus enthusiasm around the semiconductor-OEM diversification and the pending capital raise.
